notes:
disagreement: value: structure of the service requirements: one pass splits the service into its creation, its template link and its criteria link, the other tests all in one requirement; chose the split because the request asks for the template link and the visibility restriction in their own sentences, and each can fail on its own (the cells are the same either way).
disagreement: value: structure of the case requirements: one pass splits the case into its creation and the transition to work_in_progress, the other tests both in one requirement; chose the split because the request asks for the transition as a separate step after the case is triggered, and the policy creates cases in draft (the cells are the same either way).
disagreement: value: source of the category, topic detail, template, criteria and service requirements: one pass names only the check that creates each row, the other also names the checks that join on that row's name (the topic detail and service checks on the category, the service check on the topic detail, template and criteria, the case check on the service); chose the joint carriage, since each of those checks tests a cell the requirement carries and the link to the benchmark's checks is kept.
disagreement: value: the template's change_request_values predicates: one pass anchors each mapped value to its quoted key, the other uses the benchmark's predicates; chose the key-anchored form, the tighter of two right predicates given the seed's JSON text format (resolved on that requirement).
The two passes otherwise agree on every row, id, cell and disposition (five checks kept, the criteria check repaired the same way).
All six rows are new: none of the category, topic detail, template, criteria, service or case exists in the seed, so each id is the next in its table. Requirements refer to each other's new rows by id; the benchmark's name joins are carried by the requirement that creates each named row.
The criteria's users (Joanne Simpson, user 4; Richard Lopez, user 57) are untestable because the seed shows no non-null value of the users JSON column.
The template mappings name an assignment group 'HR Tier 1' that does not exist in user_group; it is tested only as text inside the mappings.
The case's priority is left out: the request gives none, the policy defaults to moderate, and the template's mapping says high. Its short description is left out too: the template's text and the policy's 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: ' format disagree and the request fixes neither.
The acting user Karen Watkins is an administrator, and the policy says administrators must not perform routine HR case work; the case here is the test of the new configuration that the request asks for, so it is kept as a requirement.
